div.head: Hn 29.2a
div.ab: Per plegium uero dimittatur ad diem disracionandi uel emendandi; et seisiatus placitet et sit pro capitali suo; et non ducatur hoc namium extra hundretum.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 563 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: gegen Bürgschaft aber bleibe Verklagter frei bis zum Termin
but on giving surety the defendant is to remain free until the appointed day
das Erscheinen des Beklagten gelte statt seines gepfändeten Stück Vieh, d. h. hebe Pfand- und Bürgenpflicht auf
the appearance of the defendant is to count in place of his distrained beast, i.e. it cancels the obligation of pledge and surety
si K Co; fehlt Or; sic Wh
si K Co; missing in Or; sic Wh
vom Corr. umgestellt s. c. Sc; s. c. übr.
transposed by the corrector s. c. Sc; s. c. the rest

Bürgschaft befreit von Pfändung (s. d. Gl 14a), und Beklagter braucht nur nach Herausgabe des Abgepfändeten zu antworten; sonst hätte er die (von kanonischer exceptio spolii beeinflusste) Einrede der Entwerung; vgl. Pol Mai II 47; Maitland Coll. papers I 332

Surety frees from distraint (see that word in Gl 14a), and the defendant need answer only after restitution of what was distrained; otherwise he would have the plea of disseisin (influenced by the canonical exceptio spolii); cf. Pol Mai II 47; Maitland Coll. papers I 332

Als Missbrauch beklagt chacier naam hors del hundred Mirror of justices V 1, 78 ed. Whitaker 164.—Am Rande spät: Nota, districtiones [abgepfändete Fahrhabe] non ducendas extra hundretum—suo captali{27}—hoc{28} fehlt Rs

chacier naam hors del hundred is complained of as an abuse in Mirror of justices V 1, 78 ed. Whitaker 164. — In the margin, in a late hand: Nota, districtiones [distrained chattels] non ducendas extra hundretum — suo captali{27} — hoc{28} missing Rs

div.ab: But let it be released on pledge until the day for deraigning or making amends; and let him plead [being] seised [of it], and let it count as his principal [?]; and let this distress not be taken outside the hundred.
